source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Carrollton publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet, ranking third among Texas data centers that disclose power and accounting for 9.5 percent of the state's published load.

At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this translates to roughly 1,100 racks, or 4,400 to 8,800 H100-equivalent accelerators at typical hyperscaler utilization. That is a substantial compute footprint, but the certifications and operator type point to general colocation rather than a dedicated AI training cluster, and no tenant workloads are published.

Only 19 of 133 mapped Texas data centers publish power figures, so this campus is one of a small transparent minority; most state capacity remains undisclosed. The suitability score of 71 is incomplete because no announced expansion is recorded, and no tenant, address, or airport data is published. Certifications such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, and FISMA qualify the site for regulated workloads but say nothing about AI-specific compute, and the data does not include grid connection details, so it cannot show whether this campus is power-constrained.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
